categories.reasoning: Comprehensive coverage of 12 categories with 40 rules synthesizing best practices from Microsoft, Zalando, and PayPal. Covers all essential domains: naming (snake_case), URLs, HTTP methods/status, errors (RFC 7807), pagination (cursor-based), versioning (URI prefix), security (OAuth 2.0), and documentation.

Excellent structure with PO-XXX rule IDs, 12 logical categories, conformance levels (minimum/standard/exemplary), and clear TOC. Rules progress naturally from general principles through specific implementation details.

Each rule includes ID, title, severity, description, rationale, and source attribution. Clear MUST/SHOULD language with RFC 2119 semantics. Rationale explains why each choice was made, citing source guidelines.
Good/bad examples provided for most rules. Examples are concise and practical. Could benefit from more complete OpenAPI snippets showing full endpoint definitions.

findings.recommendation: Add full endpoint examples showing headers, parameters, request/response bodies together

categories.reasoning: Clear separation between Spectral-lintable rules (deterministic) and LLM-judge rules (semantic). Generated .spectral.yaml provides ready-to-use linting. Generated .rubric.json enables automated LLM evaluation.
Covers API versioning with URI prefix (/v1/) and deprecation with Sunset header. Could expand on guide evolution process itself - how the PlexusOne guidelines will be versioned and updated.

categories.reasoning: Excellent depth for a synthesized guide: RFC 7807 errors, cursor pagination with next_cursor, rate limit headers (RateLimit-*), security with OAuth scopes, filtering with operators. Draws from three mature guideline sources.

Fully consistent: snake_case everywhere (properties, query params), kebab-case for URLs, /v1/ prefix versioning, RFC 7807 errors. No contradictions between rules. Clear opinionated choices documented.

Clear, concise writing suitable for developers. Avoids jargon while maintaining technical precision. Source attributions help developers understand lineage. Three conformance levels support gradual adoption.
